title: This Fish Still Has a Tongue. It Just Isn't Its Own

scenes.text: This fish still uses its tongue. It just isn't its own.
A crustacean the size of a tick swims in through the gills and clamps onto the tongue.
It cuts the blood supply. The tongue withers and drops off, and the louse grips the stump.
It grows to about an inch and simply does the tongue's job. The fish keeps eating.
It is the only animal known to replace another's body part, form and function.
It drinks the fish's blood for up to three years. So, whose tongue is it now?

description:
A fish that still has a working tongue, except the tongue is a living parasite.
The tongue-eating louse (Cymothoa exigua) enters a snapper through its gills, cuts off the blood supply to the tongue until it falls away, then grips the stump and takes over the job. It grows to about an inch, feeds on the fish's blood and mucus, and can live up to three years; the fish keeps eating normally. It is the only animal known to replace another animal's body part in both form and function.
What is the strangest parasite you have ever heard of?
subject: tongue-eating louse
first_comment: The louse starts life as a male; the first one into a fish turns female and takes the tongue's place. Which parasite would you least like to meet?
